newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak FinMin to push for changes in GDP structure.
newsitem.headline: Slovak FinMin to push for changes in GDP structure.

text.p: The Slovak government will push for changes in the structure of the economy in 1997, to ensure healthier and sustainable economic growth in the future, Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said on Thursday.

"We will try to pursue changes in the structure of GDP in 1997, mainly by boosting exports of more sophisticated products with a higher added value and reducing expensive and unprofitable imports," Kozlik told an economic roundtable.
He said the process should help the economy to achieve a healthier structure in the long-term, and will require financing from both domestic and foreign sources.
"Economic restructuring will require around 1,000 billion crowns in investments by the year 2000, and can come in all possible forms," Kozlik said.
Slovakia has enjoyed strong economic growth led by domestic demand over the past few years, with the real 1996 GDP rising 6.9 percent year-on-year, after a 6.8 percent increase in 1995.

"This restructuring is the reason why we are pushing for such quick motorway construction and other infrastructure projetcs, since the infrastructure will create a solid basis for the entry of foreign investment," Kozlik said.
He repeated the finance ministry's forecast of real GDP growth of at least six percent in 1997.

Kozlik added that he saw enough political will to proceed with the privatisation of so-called strategic industries after the 1998 general elections, but did not say whether the current government was already working on such sell-offs.
The government list of strategic companies includes some of the largest state enterprises, such as gas distributor SPP and Slovak Telecom.
Kozlik said the government was considering both direct sales and equity increases through strategic investors for privatisation, adding that so far the latter option looked more favourable.
